questions.q: What makes a Fabric Warehouse different from a Lakehouse's engine model?
options: A Warehouse is SQL-first, with full T-SQL as its native language, rather than a Spark-first item with a SQL endpoint bolted on
A Warehouse doesn't use OneLake storage at all, unlike a Lakehouse
A Warehouse can only read data, never write it
A Warehouse and Lakehouse are functionally identical with no real difference
questions.explain: The engine on top differs, but the underlying storage — Delta in OneLake — doesn't.

questions.q: What kind of T-SQL operations does a Fabric Warehouse support?
options: The full surface — CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, real multi-statement transactions
Only SELECT statements, exactly like a Lakehouse's SQL endpoint
Only stored procedures, no direct table operations
Only read-only queries against externally managed tables
questions.explain: This is the full T-SQL surface the track's own T-SQL course built up over 118 lessons.

questions.q: Why can't a Lakehouse's SQL endpoint support real INSERT/UPDATE statements the way a Warehouse can?
options: The SQL endpoint provides read-only access to Spark-managed Delta tables, unlike a Warehouse's SQL-first, write-capable design
Lakehouses don't have a SQL endpoint at all
INSERT/UPDATE statements are technically impossible in T-SQL generally
There's no real difference; both support identical write operations
questions.explain: This is exactly the distinction described between Lesson 5's Lakehouse SQL endpoint and this lesson's Warehouse.

questions.q: How does a Fabric Warehouse relate to this track's standalone T-SQL course?
options: It's the place that T-SQL skill set becomes directly relevant to data engineering work — the same syntax, applied to a Fabric warehouse table
It has no relationship to the T-SQL course at all
It replaces the need for the T-SQL course entirely
It only supports a small subset of T-SQL, unrelated to what that course taught
questions.explain: This genuinely completes the circle back to a course from earlier in this track.

questions.q: Where does a Fabric Warehouse's actual table data live?
options: In OneLake, in Delta format — the same underlying storage a Lakehouse uses
In a completely separate SQL Server instance unrelated to OneLake
Only in memory, with no persistent storage
In a proprietary Fabric-only format distinct from Delta
questions.explain: The engine on top (SQL-first vs. Spark-first) differs; the storage underneath is the same OneLake-backed Delta.
